metaDescription: Upright vacuums under $200 from Shark, Kenmore, Oreck and Bissell compared by bags, pods, HEPA seals and parts support, so the budget buys a lasting machine.
expertTake: The Shark Navigator Lift-Away ZU561 is the best upright under $200 because it adds a self-cleaning brushroll, a lift-away pod and a complete seal to a proven platform. The Kenmore Intuition is the pick if you want a bag. Skip this band if you need a heavy-duty machine for plush wall-to-wall carpet; the stronger motors sit above the cap.
introParagraphs: This is the price band where uprights from established makers appear: pods that lift away, sealed housings and bags that release with a button. The motors are still mid-sized, but the features around them solve real chores.

What the extra budget buys over the cheapest machines is convenience and parts support, not deep-pile power. The cap of $200 reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, and prices move, so check the current figure before you buy.

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away Speed ZU561, self-cleaning roll, HEPA

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA, over 99.9 percent of dust and allergens

products.description:
The ZU561 packs three useful ideas into a mid-priced upright. A self-cleaning brushroll strips pet hair as it works, so you avoid the scissors chore that plagues cheaper rolls. A lift-away pod gives you a lighter unit for stairs and furniture, and the maker says an anti-allergen complete seal with a HEPA filter traps over 99.9 percent of dust and allergens.

Next to the Navigator NV352 it adds the self-cleaning roll and the seal, and next to the Kenmore Intuition it uses a cup rather than a bag. That makes it cheaper to run, though emptying the cup releases some dust.

The seal depends on rubber gaskets, so inspect them every few months for cracks and keep the cup seat clean. Wash the foam and felt filters monthly and let them dry for a full day, check the roll ends for the odd strand and wipe the pod joint with a dry cloth. Seat the pod until it clicks, because a half-seated pod leaks air and the machine seems weak. Empty the cup outdoors into a bag held tight to the opening, since a sealed machine still releases a puff of fine dust when the cup opens, and rinse the cup now and then, letting it dry completely so no damp film builds on the walls. If you have a long-haired pet, expect to glance at the roll ends every month, because even a self-cleaning roll lets a few strands reach the bearing, and a roll that no longer turns freely loads the belt and shortens its life.
products.bestFor: Pet homes that want a self-cleaning roll, a pod and a stated seal.
cons: Bagless cup releases dust when emptied

products.name: Kenmore Intuition bagged lift-up upright, pet friendly, 2-motor

specList.label: Emptying
specList.value: Single button releases the full bag

specList.label: Suction
specList.value: Strong even as the bag fills

products.description:
A bag changes how dust is handled: you press one button and the full bag drops out, so you never touch the dirt. The Intuition pairs that with a 200 watt lift-up pod for stairs and above-floor cleaning and a two-motor system that the maker designs to hold suction as the bag fills.

It is a pet-friendly bagged upright, so it suits a house that wants dust contained. Next to the ZU561 it trades the self-cleaning roll for a bag, and bags are a recurring cost.

Buy spare bags in the right style and keep them with the vacuum, seat each bag flat and close the door until it clicks, because a crooked bag leaks into the housing. Wipe the pod joint monthly, check the roll for hair and replace any washable filter on the manual's schedule. A bag change is cleaner than emptying a cup, but only if you do it before the bag packs solid. The pod is the place most owners get frustrated, so learn the release motion in the shop or on the first day, work from the top step down on stairs and carry the pod with the hose clipped back, which stops the hose dragging on each tread. A pet household should check the pod hose for hair plugs when suction drops, because a plug looks exactly like a failing motor and is cleared in a minute with a broom handle.
products.bestFor: Households that want dust contained and a pod for stairs.
cons: Pod joint is an extra seal to keep clean

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL bagged upright, 9 lb, auto height
products.description:
The XL is a nine pound commercial bagged upright with automatic height adjustment, so it handles carpet and hard floor without a dial. A high-speed brush roll provides the agitation, and a bag collects the dirt.

It is the lightest machine in this guide and the simplest, which is why it has stayed in janitor closets for years. Next to the Kenmore Intuition it has no pod, but it is lighter and cheaper to repair.

Change the bag at two thirds full, replace the belt on schedule and check the brush for thread. The height mechanism can clog with lint, so tilt the machine back and clear the base plate every month, and park it standing, since a very light body tips easily. Because it has been a janitor-closet staple, spares are easy to find, so buy a couple of belts and a pack of bags with it and keep them in a labelled bag on the closet wall. A very light upright skims over thick pile, so go slowly on rugs and make overlapping passes, and do not use it for wet spills, sand or drywall dust, which clog a thin bag and cut through the paper in minutes, leaving the motor coated in fine grit.
products.bestFor: Busy homes and small offices that want a light, simple machine.

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away NV352, DuoClean PowerFins, HEPA

specList.label: Hair
specList.value: Pet hair pickup with no wrap

products.description:
The NV352 uses a DuoClean PowerFins head that combines two brushrolls, a PowerFins roll and a soft roller, so it digs into carpet and sweeps hard floors in one pass. An easy-release pedal detaches the lightweight pod, and a HEPA filter cleans the exhaust.

Next to the ZU561 it has the two-roll head but not the complete seal, and next to the Oreck XL it is heavier and better at pet hair. A mixed home gets solid value from it.

Step on the pedal to release the pod and set it down gently, wash the filters monthly and check the roll ends for hair. The soft roller collects fine dust and hair at its ends, so lift it out when the manual allows and wipe it with a damp cloth. The two-roll head is gentler on hard floors than a single stiff bar because the soft roller cushions the contact, which matters if part of your home is wood, but remember that neither roll can be switched off, so a polished plank is better served by the pod nozzle and a slow pass. Seat the pod firmly after use and check that the pedal moves freely, since lint under it is the usual cause of a stiff release.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors with pets that want the two-roll head.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Swivel Pet 2252, triple action roll
products.description:
The 2252 is a pet-oriented swivel upright with a triple action brush roll, scatter-free technology for hard floors and a large tank. Swivel steering lets it turn around furniture without lifting.

Next to the NV352 it has no pod but better steering, and next to the ZU561 it lacks the seal and the self-cleaning roll. It is an older design, so confirm that belts and filters are sold.

Every two weeks, snip hair off the roll, empty the tank before it fills and rinse the filter monthly. Tilt the machine back and clear the swivel joint of thread now and then. A stiff pivot undoes the steering that is the reason to buy this model, and it tempts you to drag the head, which strains the wheels and the belt. The scatter-free feature works best at a steady pace on hard floors, so avoid quick strokes, and when the tank is packed with fur, wash it in warm water and let it dry completely before refitting, since damp fur holds odor. Keep a spare belt, because parts for an older design thin out over time.
products.bestFor: Cluttered rooms with pets and a mix of surfaces.

products.name: Kenmore lightweight bagless upright, 4 heights, Pet HandiMate

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Pet HandiMate and two cleaning tools

products.description:
Four height levels set the head for the floor, and a weight under 12 pounds keeps it manageable. It includes the Pet HandiMate and two cleaning tools for stairs and upholstery.

Next to the Intuition it is bagless and has no pod, so it is cheaper to run and simpler. It suits a home that wants a plain, light upright.

Set the height when you change rooms, empty the cup before it fills and wash the filter monthly. A height dial left on the lowest setting is the commonest reason this model seems to push hard. A good rule is the lowest setting for a rug, the next for low-pile carpet and the top two for tile and hardwood, with a glance at the head each time you change rooms. If the machine starts to feel as if it is dragging, raise the height one notch before you suspect a fault, and keep the Pet HandiMate on the handle so that stairs and the sofa never send you looking for a separate tool.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors where you will set the height by hand.
cons: Height must be set by hand

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Shark ZU561 lists an anti-allergen complete seal with HEPA, and the Kenmore Intuition a sealed bagged system. A HEPA label without a seal lets dust bypass the filter. At this tier you can start to ask for a seal, and it is worth doing, because a sealed machine keeps fine dust inside until you empty it and an unsealed one lets some of it out every time the motor runs. Look for the statement in the listing, since makers who have built a sealed path say so.

The Kenmore Intuition and Oreck XL use bags, while the Shark and Bissell models use cups. Bags contain dust but cost money. Cups are cheaper to run but release a puff when emptied, so count a year of bags against a pair of filters when you compare running costs, and weigh both against how sensitive anyone in the home is to fine dust.

The Shark ZU561 and NV352 and the Kenmore Intuition have detachable pods. A pod saves carrying the full machine. It adds a joint that must be kept clean and seated, and a pod that is only resting in its cradle leaks air without any visible sign, so listen for the click each time you refit it and wipe the joint with a dry cloth every month to keep lint from lifting the seal.

The ZU561 has a self-cleaning roll, the NV352 a two-roll head and the Bissell 2252 a triple action roll. Plain rolls wrap hair. Choose the roll for your pets, and treat every anti-wrap claim as a feature that reduces the chore, not one that removes it, since long hair finds a way onto any roll and a monthly look at the bearing ends is part of owning any upright.
Shark, Kenmore and Oreck sell belts, bags and filters widely, while older Bissell models can be harder to supply. Belts and filters wear out, so check that the parts for your exact model are sold.
The Oreck XL is about 9 pounds and the Kenmore lightweight under 12, while the Shark pod machines are heavier. A machine you can lift gets used. Match the weight to your stairs.

faq.q: What does this cap buy that the cheapest uprights do not?
faq.a: Pods, seals and bags from makers with parts support. It does not buy plush-carpet power, so the motors are still mid-sized, and the real gains are convenience features and the confidence that belts, bags and filters will still be on sale in three years when you need them.

faq.q: Does the $200 cap reflect current prices?
faq.a: Each machine was under the cap at the last update; because listings change, verify the price on the day you shop.

faq.q: Is a sealed bagless machine good for allergies?
faq.a: If it has a complete seal, yes, but empty the cup outdoors.
Bagged contains dust better and costs money for bags. Bagless is cheaper to run.
They are maker figures for the filter chain. A sealed housing matters as much.

Several years with belts and filters replaced. Brands with parts supply last longest, because a machine is only as durable as the cheapest part you cannot buy, and a vacuum with no belts on sale is a vacuum with a fixed end date.
